<!--

  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the

This PR fixes a bug parsing due dates for calendar events.  If the due date had no time data, it was incorrectly parsed as UTC with time data.  Which, based on your timezone, would put the task in the wrong date and show time data, rather than an all day event.

It also fixes an unrelated bug I noticed, where the create new task service failed to create a task due to a bad date format string in the integration.

issue_context.title: Todoist Integratio Timezone Issues in Calendar
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I primarily use Todoist with tasks due on a day, as opposed to a specific time.  It looks like it sets those as due at the end of the day, which works correctly for me on todoist.com.  However, in Home Assistant's calendar, every task that is due on a day is due at 16:00 on the previous day, which matches my UTC offset of -8 in Pacific Standard Time.

Initially, I thought this was #59715 (fixed with #60038), but I'm pretty sure that should be live in the version of Home Assistant that I'm running, so it seemed like a good idea to open a new issue.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.12.10

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

todoist

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/todoist/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

For a concrete example, I currently have a task due on Tuesday, February 1st, 2022.  However, the calendar view in Home Assistant shows this task due on Monday, January 31st, 2022 at 16:00.

My timezone is set correctly at "America/Los_Angeles" in Home Assistant, and to "(GMT-0800) Pacific Time (US & Canada)" in Todoist.
comments:
Hey there @boralyl, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`todoist`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L964) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@sdwilsh Thanks for reporting!  I don't use the calendar, but when I loaded it up in my local HA instance, I can see the problem you are reporting with my tasks due on Sunday PDT showing as due Saturday at 16:00 (which matches my UTC offset).  Since it's easily reproducible I should be able to track down the root cause.

I was setting up [mampfes/hacs_waste_collection_schedule](https://github.com/mampfes/hacs_waste_collection_schedule) today as well, and it appears to just set a date for calendar entries, which shows up exactly how I'd expect `all_day` tasks to work for this.  I can provide a screenshot if you need to see that in action.

I've narrowed down the issue, it appears calendar event dates for this integration will always be in UTC due to how they are parsed.

It will take a bit of time to untangle this code and add some tests, but I should have a pull request with a fix in the next week.
@boralyl, should this be fixed in 2022.3.x, or is it going to make it in 2022.4.x?  I'm still seeing it in 2022.3.x
@sdwilsh It's not in any of the March releases, so this should land in 2022.4.x.

review_comments: This was an unrelated bug, that caused an HTTP 400 error when POST-ed to the todoist api due to the missing colon.
This was the main issue, it ignored the user's timezone and parsed the due date as UTC with time information.
Not sure why this dict mutation was here, but it doesn't appear to have a negative effect locally when I removed it.
